Nimrod
nĭm´rŏd
n. (son of Cush; the first man Scripture calls mighty, and the founder of Babel)
Hebrew Nimrod, traditionally connected with marad, to rebel. Genesis says he began to be a mighty one in the earth, and the kingdom he began was Babel.

Biblical Definition

“And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth” (Gen 10:8). “He was a mighty hunter before the LORD: wherefore it is said, Even as Nimrod the mighty hunter before the LORD” (Gen 10:9). The next verse names what he built: “the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar” (Gen 10:10) — and the following chapter records what was said in that place: “let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name” (Gen 11:4). Chronicles repeats the genealogy (1Ch 1:10), and Micah calls Assyria “the land of Nimrod” (Mic 5:6).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a hunter as one who pursues wild animals with a view to take them, and mighty as very strong, powerful, having great command.

expand to see more

HUNTER, n. One who pursues wild animals with a view to take them, either for sport or for food.

MIGHTY, a. Having great bodily strength or physical power; very strong; powerful.

MIGHTY, n. A warrior; a chieftain of great valor or power.

Key Scripture

Gen 10:8 — "And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth."

Gen 10:9 — "He was a mighty hunter before the LORD: wherefore it is said, Even as Nimrod the mighty hunter before the LORD."

Gen 10:10 — "And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar."

Gen 11:4 — "And they said, Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth."

Modern Corruption

Nimrod is the first man in Scripture called mighty, the first to have a kingdom, and the founder of the city that becomes the Bible's standing name for organized rebellion.

expand to see more

Genesis 10:8-10 is short and heavy with consequence. Nimrod began to be a mighty one — a new thing in the earth after the flood — and the beginning of his kingdom was Babel. Genesis is careful with beginnings, and this is the beginning of empire. The stated purpose at Babel is not defence or trade but reputation and cohesion: let us make us a name, lest we be scattered — a direct refusal of the command given to Noah to replenish the earth. Babylon runs from that tower through Nebuchadnezzar to Revelation 18, and Micah still calls Assyria the land of Nimrod centuries later.

The corruption to name is the city that builds upward to make a name for itself, which is the perennial project of human civilization and not a relic of the ancient world. Augustine's two cities are drawn from this material: one founded on the love of God to the contempt of self, the other on the love of self to the contempt of God. God's answer to Babel was not destruction but confusion of language, and the reversal comes at Pentecost, where men out of every nation under heaven hear the wonderful works of God each in his own tongue. Babel gathers to make a name; the gospel scatters in the name that is above every name.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew gibbor (H1368), mighty one, warrior; tsayid (H6718), hunting, game; Babel (H894), Babel, confusion; shem (H8034), name.

expand to see more

Hebrew gibbor (H1368) — mighty one, champion; Genesis 10:8, 6:4, Psalm 45:3.

Hebrew tsayid (H6718) — hunting, game, provision; Genesis 10:9, 25:28.

Hebrew Babel (H894) — Babel, Babylon; Genesis 10:10, 11:9, Jeremiah 51:6.

Hebrew shem (H8034) — name, reputation; Genesis 11:4, Proverbs 22:1.

Hebrew Shinar (H8152) — Shinar, the plain of Babylonia; Genesis 10:10, Daniel 1:2.

Usage

"“He began to be a mighty one in the earth” — the first such man named."

"“The beginning of his kingdom was Babel” — the beginning of empire."

"“Let us make us a name” — the purpose stated at the tower."
